method: Static analysis only - javap -c -p on the named 26.1 jars (client.jar for client classes, server-game.jar for server classes) for every vanilla method in scope, Rust source reads, and prepared-data checks (items.json, block-tags.json, jar data files). NO drivers were run and NO oracle repairs were done: this batch is checks + triage only per the brief (no cargo builds, no driver runs). The 32 runnable drivers and 17 no-oracle drivers are recorded as not run, not as passes. Driver inventory: 74 drivers in the working set - 32 runnable-but-unrun, 25 blocked on 26 measured-failing oracles (Batch 0's measured table), 17 no-oracle. Oracle sets cross-checked against the 26.1 driver files; the only mismatch is interaction_input (also references the ParityData helper). Withdrawn for 26.1 (re-checked against 26.1's jar + 26.1 tree; numbers NOT reused): B7-G02 (26.1's BucketItem HAS the sneak check), B7-G05 (26.1 posts ENTITY_PLACE at the spawn position), B7-G07 (26.1 has no block_transformer registry; the port hardcodes the correct tables), B7-G08 (campfire douse implemented directly). Fixed in the 26.1 tree: B7-G16 (the port applies use_cooldown on pearl/wind-charge throw).

source: docs/PARITY-SWEEP.md §4 Batch 7 — checks + triage only, no fixes. Scope: item use, food, tools, armour, buckets, spawn eggs, components — 1,506 items. The §1.1 spec gap (block-behaviours.json holds only BlockItem entries) was resolved by extracting the item→Java-class map from the named 26.1 jar: all 1,506 items mapped to 70 classes, 0 unmapped, 0 mismatches against block-behaviours.json. The brief's assumption that spears/nautilus armour are 26.2-only families was wrong: all 7 spears and all 5 nautilus armours exist in 26.1 (verified in items.json and the jar's Items class), so B33/B34 are full checks.
systemic_note: The 26.1 story is the inverse of 26.2's in one respect and a repeat of 1.21.7's in another. In 26.2, the port authors already did the version-specific work and the 1.21.7 systemic defects were fixed or withdrawn. In 26.1, FOUR of the 1.21.7 systemic defects reproduce because the 26.1 port carries 26.2/26.3 forms for behaviours 26.1 implements differently: G09 (chorus teleport keyed on a tag that does not exist in 26.1), G10 (splash-water gated on potion tags that do not exist in 26.1), G11 (the convertable/convertible misspelling), and G01 (the component_patch error 26.2 fixed but 26.1 did not). The 26.1 port is also OLDER than 26.2's in the oracle layer: six drivers that were runnable in 26.2 are blocked here, mostly on 26.2-form APIs (Level.getNextEntityId, the ClockInstance, EntityTypes registration, 5-arg randomTeleport). The counter-example is G16: the 26.1 tree already applies use_cooldown on pearl/wind-charge throw, a fix 26.2's tree lacked - version-specific work in 26.1 is uneven, not uniformly behind.
